latin_text: Hic est nodus primarum mentium, ordo Palladicus philosophiae contemplativae preses; hic nobis et emulandus primo et ambiendus, atque adeo comprehendendus est
english_translation: The cherub is the bond of the Prime Minds, the order of Pallas, the overseer of contemplative philosophy. First we must emulate him, thirst after him and to the same degree understand him
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico identifies the Cherub as *nodus primarum mentium*—the knot or bond of the Prime Minds—and as the celestial exemplar of *Palladica philosophia*, the wisdom tradition represented by Pallas Athena. [INFERRED] The Cherub occupies a structural position as the mediating order between the Thrones (divine executive power) and the lower orders. More importantly, Cherubim are characterized by the fullness of divine knowledge (*plenitudo scientiae*), the comprehensive vision that holds together all intelligible forms. The passage establishes the Cherub as the cosmic principle of mediation and unity-in-multiplicity: the Cherub contemplates the divine ideas in their wholeness and simultaneously illuminates all lower orders through hierarchical gradation.

The philosophical function is to model human philosophical practice on the cherubic order. Just as Cherubim contemplate the totality of divine ideas and mediate between the transcendent God and the cosmos, human philosophers must emulate this integrative role: holding together intellectual disciplines (logic, physics, metaphysics), mediating between theoretical and practical knowledge, and ultimately directing the lower orders (desires, imagination, sensation) toward participation in divine wisdom. The phrase *ordo Palladicus philosophiae contemplativae preses* suggests that true philosophy is not merely abstract reasoning but a contemplative order organized hierarchically like the angelic Cherubim. *Emulandi primo et ambiendus* (to be emulated first and sought after)—the Cherub is the primary exemplar because the Cherub is the order of mediation itself, the archetypal mediator between transcendence and immanence.

[INFERRED] Heptaplus 6.6 elaborates the role of Cherubim in the cosmological order as governors of knowledge and illumination. The Commento Book I-II describes how the angelic Intellect (second hypostasis) functions exactly as Pico describes Cherubim: as the mediation and bond holding together all lower realities. Being & Unity grounds this metaphysically: the Cherub exemplifies participated intellectual being—the capacity to receive, hold, and communicate divine knowledge in hierarchical gradations. The human philosopher, emulating the Cherub, participates in this mediating function.

other_texts: Macrobius, On the Dream of Scipio 1.6.11

notes: The cherub (second highest angel) is the philosophical mediator, the bond between highest and lower orders. Human philosophy must be organized on the cherubic model—contemplative, mediating, hierarchical.
